raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Test-only change. `simulate_tool_streaming()` gains an opt-in
`delta_token_ids_per_chunk` parameter, so tests can stream explicit per-chunk
token ids through the shared helper. `test_granite.py` and `test_inkling.py`
migrate their `_stream()` loops to it. Fixes #65328.

## Claims

- `simulate_tool_streaming(parser, request, chunks,
  delta_token_ids_per_chunk=...)` streams explicit per-chunk delta ids, one
  entry per chunk. Example: the full per-token ids serving sends. This mirrors
  the existing escape hatch of `simulate_reasoning_streaming()`.
- Default behavior is unchanged. Without the parameter, the helper synthesizes
  marker-only ids from the chunk text exactly as before. None of the eight
  existing callers change.
- `test_granite.py` and `test_inkling.py` now stream through the helper with
  explicit ids. Their old `_stream()` loops already built token-batched ids
  plus a final `finish_streaming()`, so the call sequence is unchanged.

## Validation

No model evaluation. The change touches test files only.

Fails before / passes after:

- The new test cannot run on base, because the parameter does not exist
  there. The fails-before evidence is the #65328 repro on base `380c8e438c`
  (short version):

```text
A. helper-shaped delta_token_ids: 1 call(s)    # first call dropped
B. serving-shaped delta_token_ids: 2 call(s)   # both calls parse
```

- With this patch, I ran the commands below on main @ `9b14bef3be` (branch
  `tests-helper-token-ids`). The tests/parser/engine tree is identical to
  `380c8e438c`, where the repro ran. Python 3.12.13, pytest 9.1.0, CPU-only.

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_streaming_helpers.py -v
# 4 passed, 14 warnings in 0.08s (1 unit + 3 parametrized)
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_granite.py tests/parser/engine/test_inkling.py -q
# 125 passed, 14 warnings in 0.57s
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine -q
# 6097 passed, 14 warnings in 20.43s
```

The 14 warnings are `torch.jit.script_method` deprecation noise from
importing torch. The full-suite run covers the eight pre-existing helper
callers, so the default path is unchanged there too.

- New `tests/parser/engine/test_streaming_helpers.py`:
  - streams full per-token ids for the layout where the synthesized
    marker-only ids drop the first tool call (the #65328 reproducer), and
    asserts both calls parse.
  - asserts explicit ids match the synthesized default and the expected calls
    on well-formed layouts (whole / between-calls / char-by-char).
- Lint: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the four changed
  files. Version: ruff 0.14.0, the repo's pre-commit rev (`f9351c92`).
- CI: the `misc` step runs `pytest -v -s parser`
  (`.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`), which includes the new file.
- Paired sweep data from #65328 (same input family, 296 layouts = 3 named
  chunkings + every binary split):

| delta id stream | layouts failing |
|---|---|
| helper-synthesized (marker-only, deduplicated) | 134 / 296 |
| helper-synthesized + final `finish_streaming()` | 134 / 296 (identical count and the same first five failing layouts) |
| full per-token ids (serving style) | 0 / 296 |

Serving never splits inside a multi-character marker, because tokens are
atomic there. The failing set also contains token-aligned splits such as
split@12–16, so the conclusion does not depend on the marker-internal splits.

## Details

The synthesized ids are marker-only, deduplicated, and carry no ids for
ordinary text. When a delta mixes a marker with ordinary text, its ids are
not a tokenization of the delta text, and serving never sends ids like that.

The production bridge (`ParserEngineToolAdapter.extract_tool_calls_streaming`)
passes `delta_token_ids` through unchanged. With `--stream-interval N > 1`,
each delta carries a batch of N full per-token ids. #45256 is the bug class
that only shows up under that batching.

Serving keeps one rule: `delta_token_ids` is a tokenization of `delta_text`.
The helper cannot keep that rule from text alone. Once any ids arrive, the
engine trusts the token ids and stops matching their text.

On the #64012 input family, 134/296 chunk layouts fail under the synthesized
ids. Full per-token ids parse all 296.

The text-only interface also cannot feed token batches, so the suite works
around it by hand:

- test_granite.py, test_inkling.py, and llama_json build their own
  `delta_token_ids` and call `extract_tool_calls_streaming` in a loop. The
  first two migrate here.
- gemma4's token-batched tests (including the detokenizer-holdback ones) and
  `replay_harness.py` go through `parse_delta()` instead, which already takes
  ids.
- The same marker-only id construction is also copy-pasted into two `_stream*`
  helpers in `test_parser_engine.py` (both call `parse_delta()`).

Design:

- The parameter mirrors the reasoning-side hatch. When explicit ids are
  given, the helper skips the token-id map, so the two helpers stay symmetric.
- Encoding the chunks inside the helper does not work for current callers.
  Many pass Mock tokenizers whose `encode()` returns a constant, so the
  per-chunk ids have to come from the caller.
- The default synthesis stays unchanged, because the eight existing test
  files that call the helper rely on the current token-id coverage. The new
  tests do not encode the default mode's divergence into assertions: they
  assert the explicit mode's correctness, and mode agreement on green layouts
  only.

granite and inkling migrate here. llama_json's `_stream()` is the same kind
of loop, so it can follow the same way. The `parse_delta()`-based feeders use
a different API and stay as they are.

Duplicate check (2026-11-03): apart from #65328 (the issue this PR fixes), no
open PR or issue mentions `streaming_helpers` or `delta_token_ids_per_chunk`.
`simulate_tool_streaming` appears only in #46274 (related, non-competing)
and closed #58505 (MiniMax think mode, unrelated).

AI assistance: this change and its description were prepared with AI
assistance. All commands and quoted results were run by me on main @
`9b14bef3be` plus this patch. The #65328 repro ran on `380c8e438c`, and the
tests/parser/engine tree is identical between the two commits.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tests for the shared streaming simulation helpers."""
+
+import json
+
+import pytest
+
+from tests.parser.engine.streaming_helpers import simulate_tool_streaming
+from vllm.parser.engine.parser_engine import ParserEngine
+from vllm.parser.qwen3 import TOOL_CALL_END, TOOL_CALL_START, qwen3_config
+
+FUNC_OPEN = "<function=read_file>"
+PARAM_DESC_OPEN = "<parameter=description>"
+PARAM_PATH_OPEN = "<parameter=path>"
+PARAM_CLOSE = "</parameter>"
+FUNC_CLOSE = "</function>"
+
+
+class ConsistentTokenizer:
+    """Tool-call markers encode to single special ids; every other character
+    encodes to its own regular id, so decode(encode(text)) == text."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self._vocab = {TOOL_CALL_START: 100, TOOL_CALL_END: 101}
+        self._by_id = {100: TOOL_CALL_START, 101: TOOL_CALL_END}
+
+    def get_vocab(self) -> dict[str, int]:
+        return dict(self._vocab)
+
+    @property
+    def all_special_tokens(self) -> list[str]:
+        return list(self._vocab)
+
+    @property
+    def all_special_ids(self) -> list[int]:
+        return list(self._vocab.values())
+
+    def encode(self, text: str, add_special_tokens: bool = False) -> list[int]:
+        ids: list[int] = []
+        i = 0
+        while i < len(text):
+            for marker, tid in self._vocab.items():
+                if text.startswith(marker, i):
+                    ids.append(tid)
+                    i += len(marker)
+                    break
+            else:
+                ids.append(256 + ord(text[i]))
+                i += 1
+        return ids
+
+    def decode(self, ids: list[int]) -> str:
+        parts: list[str] = []
+        for tid in ids:
+            if tid in self._by_id:
+                parts.append(self._by_id[tid])
+            elif 256 <= tid < 256 + 0x110000:
+                parts.append(chr(tid - 256))
+        return "".join(parts)
+
+
+def _xml_call(description: str, path: str) -> str:
+    return (
+        TOOL_CALL_START
+        + FUNC_OPEN
+        + f"{PARAM_DESC_OPEN}{description}{PARAM_CLOSE}"
+        + f"{PARAM_PATH_OPEN}{path}{PARAM_CLOSE}"
+        + FUNC_CLOSE
+        + TOOL_CALL_END
+    )
+
+
+def _two_call_input() -> tuple[str, list[dict]]:
+    raw = _xml_call("Read first file", "/tmp/first.txt") + _xml_call(
+        "Read second file", "/tmp/second.txt"
+    )
+    expected = [
+        {
+            "name": "read_file",
+            "arguments": {
+                "description": "Read first file",
+                "path": "/tmp/first.txt",
+            },
+        },
+        {
+            "name": "read_file",
+            "arguments": {
+                "description": "Read second file",
+                "path": "/tmp/second.txt",
+            },
+        },
+    ]
+    return raw, expected
+
+
+def _new_parser() -> ParserEngine:
+    return ParserEngine(
+        ConsistentTokenizer(),
+        parser_engine_config=qwen3_config(thinking=False),
+    )
+
+
+def _streamed_calls(parser, request, chunks, delta_token_ids_per_chunk=None):
+    """Stream ``chunks`` through the helper and return the parsed calls."""
+    deltas = [
+        delta
+        for delta, _current in simulate_tool_streaming(
+            parser, request, chunks, delta_token_ids_per_chunk
+        )
+    ]
+    deltas.append(parser.finish_streaming())
+    calls: dict[int, dict] = {}
+    for delta in deltas:
+        if delta and delta.tool_calls:
+            for tc in delta.tool_calls:
+                entry = calls.setdefault(tc.index, {"name": "", "arguments": ""})
+                if tc.function:
+                    if tc.function.name:
+                        entry["name"] += tc.function.name
+                    if tc.function.arguments:
+                        entry["arguments"] += tc.function.arguments
+    return [
+        {"name": calls[i]["name"], "arguments": json.loads(calls[i]["arguments"])}
+        for i in sorted(calls)
+    ]
+
+
+def test_explicit_token_ids_parse_layout_that_synthesized_ids_drop(mock_request):
+    """Streaming real per-token ids parses a layout where the synthesized
+    marker-only ids drop the first tool call."""
+    raw, expected = _two_call_input()
+    # Chunk 1 ends just past the start marker: with the default marker-only
+    # ids the engine has already switched to token-id-authoritative matching
+    # and drops the first call (see #65328); explicit ids reproduce serving and
+    # keep both.
+    split = len(TOOL_CALL_START) + 1
+    chunks = [raw[:split], raw[split:]]
+    tokenizer = ConsistentTokenizer()
+    assert (
+        _streamed_calls(
+            _new_parser(),
+            mock_request,
+            chunks,
+            [tuple(tokenizer.encode(chunk)) for chunk in chunks],
+        )
+        == expected
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("layout", ["whole", "between_calls", "char_by_char"])
+def test_explicit_ids_match_synthesized_ids_on_well_formed_layouts(
+    mock_request, layout
+):
+    """Explicit per-chunk ids agree with the synthesized default and with the
+    expected calls on layouts both modes parse correctly."""
+    raw, expected = _two_call_input()
+    first_len = len(_xml_call("Read first file", "/tmp/first.txt"))
+    chunks = {
+        "whole": [raw],
+        "between_calls": [raw[:first_len], raw[first_len:]],
+        "char_by_char": list(raw),
+    }[layout]
+    tokenizer = ConsistentTokenizer()
+    per_chunk = [tuple(tokenizer.encode(chunk)) for chunk in chunks]
+    synthesized = _streamed_calls(_new_parser(), mock_request, chunks)
+    explicit = _streamed_calls(_new_parser(), mock_request, chunks, per_chunk)
+    assert synthesized == explicit == expected
